native_model: Generative semantic-compression account of episodic memory using rate-distortion / beta-VAE machinery
memory_representation_state: learned semantic model is retained model knowledge distinct from the episode latent
prediction_state: decoder-generated reconstruction is a generative readout, not a separate online coordination state
learned_parameters: encoder/decoder/generative parameters learned during model training
update_transition_rules: different beta settings alter rate-distortion tradeoff
retrieval_readout_rules: reconstruction from latent through learned decoder
prediction_generation_operators: generative decoder produces reconstruction conditional on z
learning_plasticity_rules: offline/model training learns theta/phi; delayed-memory simulations use distinct compression settings rather than proven within-trace consolidation
temporal_ordering: retention condition interpreted via compression setting
model_variants: task/domain implementations used for qualitative phenomena
negative_adverse_results: Several hyperparameters are chosen for qualitative comparison rather than uniquely identifying a biological mechanism.
Delayed recall is modeled with separate compression levels/models; this is not a demonstrated within-trace biological storage/consolidation update.
Information already lost at stronger compression cannot necessarily be recovered by converting representations.
Delay-to-beta mapping is an interpretive/calibration bridge, not a measured neural variable.
anti_conflation_assertions: latent z is a model representation and is not automatically a biological storage variable
delay condition is not a learning operator
decoder output is not the retained representation itself
learned model parameters are distinct from the current episode latent
